title: Midterm Exam Questions (Items 1–30)
subject: The Contemporary World
description: All 30 multiple-choice questions from the University of Nueva Caceres TCW Midterm Exam (Items 1–30, excluding the essay), with verified answers and explanations.

questions.question: This is a globalization theory which refers to the creation of various cultural practices, new economies and political groups because of the interaction of elements from different societies in the world.
options: Homogeneity
Heterogeneity
Global Value Chain
Globalization
questions.answer: Heterogeneity
questions.explanation: Cultural heterogeneity emphasizes how cross-cultural interactions generate diverse hybrid practices, economies, and groupings rather than sameness.

questions.question: This refers to the movement of people, things, places and information brought by the growing 'porosity' of global limitations.
options: Solidity
Liquidity
Flows
Glocalization
questions.answer: Flows
questions.explanation: In Bauman/Ritzer's framework, 'flows' are the actual movements of people, things, places, and information across increasingly porous barriers.

questions.question: This refers to a system of unequally powerful and competing states in which no single state is capable of imposing control on all others.
options: Interstate
Interdependent
Interaction
Interest
questions.answer: Interstate
questions.explanation: The interstate system (Wallerstein) describes competing sovereign states of unequal power where no single state rules all others.

questions.question: This is the concept of strengthening the capacity of information processing and communication made possible by technological innovations.
options: Informationalism
Glocalization
Globalization
Globalism
questions.answer: Informationalism
questions.explanation: Manuel Castells defined informationalism as the technological paradigm centered on ICT-driven information processing and communication.

questions.question: Which from the given options is a major assumption of those who are skeptical about Globalization?
options: Globalization affects the whole world uniformly
Globalization explains world trading patterns
Global institutions play an effective role in global governance
Globalization is piecemeal and fragmented in its impact and effects
questions.answer: Globalization is piecemeal and fragmented in its impact and effects
questions.explanation: Skeptics argue globalization is uneven, regionalized, and fragmented rather than uniform or all-encompassing.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is NOT true about globalization?
options: Globalization is a process of interaction and integration among the people, companies and governments of different nations, driven by international trade and investment and aided by information technology
Globalization is a recent phenomenon which traces its origin in the Information Age and thrived because of the presence of social media and new technologies
Globalization represents the global integration of international trade, investment, information technology and cultures
Globalization is the free movement of goods, services and people across the world in a seamless and integrated manner
questions.answer: Globalization is a recent phenomenon which traces its origin in the Information Age and thrived because of the presence of social media and new technologies
questions.explanation: Globalization is NOT purely recent—historical trade routes like the Silk Road and Manila Galleon Trade existed centuries before social media.

questions.question: The entry of a foreign business to a developing country has what usual effect from the given options?
options: Provides competition to local businesses
Alters the culture of the developing country
Allows the developing country to compete globally
Motivates economic reforms
questions.answer: Provides competition to local businesses
questions.explanation: Foreign MNCs entering a developing market directly introduce competition for domestic firms.

questions.question: Which scenario most clearly reflects a political indicator of globalization?
options: A fashion trend spreading from Korea to Europe via social media.
Several countries signing a multilateral agreement to address climate change.
Citizens of a country protesting against rising prices of imported goods.
A musician collaborating with international artists on a global music platform.
questions.answer: Several countries signing a multilateral agreement to address climate change.
questions.explanation: Intergovernmental multilateral treaties and diplomacy are core indicators of political globalization.

questions.question: One characteristic of globalization is the increasing interdependence of national economies. Which situation best illustrates a negative consequence of this interdependence?
options: A country receiving foreign investment to build local infrastructure.
A global financial crisis causing widespread unemployment in multiple countries.
A developing nation exporting agricultural goods to a wealthier country.
A student studying abroad on a scholarship.
questions.answer: A global financial crisis causing widespread unemployment in multiple countries.
questions.explanation: Financial contagion demonstrates how economic shocks in one market spread rapidly to connected economies.

questions.question: According to Robert Cox, 'the characteristics of globalization trend include the internationalizing of production, the new international division of labor, new migratory movements from South to North, the new competitive environment that accelerates these processes, and the internationalizing of the states... making states into agencies of the globalizing world.' This is what kind of definition of Globalization?
options: Broad and inclusive
Narrow and exclusive
Limited and specific
None of the given options
questions.answer: Broad and inclusive
questions.explanation: Robert Cox's definition spans production, labor, migration, competition, and states, making it a broad and inclusive definition.

questions.question: Which of the following situations best illustrates an indicator of economic globalization?
options: A nation implementing strict tariffs to protect local industries.
A multinational corporation outsourcing its manufacturing to another country to reduce costs.
A local community using traditional barter systems to exchange goods.
A government promoting local tourism through cultural festivals.
questions.answer: A multinational corporation outsourcing its manufacturing to another country to reduce costs.
questions.explanation: Cross-border manufacturing outsourcing by MNCs is a hallmark of economic globalization.

questions.question: Which statement is true about the Global Economy from the given options?
options: It allows countries to access resources they do not have access to
It limits the options of countries in terms of who to trade with
It allows only rich countries to trade
It is unfair all the time on poor countries
questions.answer: It allows countries to access resources they do not have access to
questions.explanation: International trade enables countries to acquire resources, goods, and technologies unavailable domestically.

questions.question: An artist who collaborates with musicians from different continents to create a new song, which is then released on a global streaming platform, is participating in:
options: Economic globalization.
Political globalization.
Technological isolation.
Cultural globalization.
questions.answer: Cultural globalization.
questions.explanation: Cross-border artistic and musical collaboration shared globally exemplifies cultural globalization.

questions.question: When examining the role of international financial institutions, which perspective argues that global market forces have fundamentally eroded the autonomy of national governments, making the nation-state an 'intermediate' and increasingly obsolete layer of governance?
options: Protectionism
Skepticism
Transformationalism
Hyperglobalism
questions.answer: Hyperglobalism
questions.explanation: Hyperglobalists contend global markets overpower nation-states, rendering traditional state sovereignty increasingly obsolete.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is NOT true?
options: The International Monetary Fund and World Bank are specialized agencies in the United Nations system

All International Financial Institutions admit only sovereign countries as owner-members, and are characterized by broad membership including both borrowing developing countries and developed donor countries
Each IFI has its own independent legal and operational status, and high cooperation is maintained through overlapping country memberships
Membership in the regional development banks is limited to countries from the region
questions.answer: Membership in the regional development banks is limited to countries from the region
questions.explanation: Regional development banks (such as ADB, AfDB, and IDB) include non-regional developed donor members like the US, Japan, and European states.

questions.question: A developing country that opens its markets to international corporations may experience rapid economic growth but could also see local industries struggle to compete. This scenario most likely presents a trade-off between:
options: Economic stability and cultural preservation.
Economic growth and income inequality.
Domestic production and consumer choice.
Technological advancement and environmental protection.
questions.answer: Domestic production and consumer choice.
questions.explanation: Opening markets gives consumers wider foreign goods and fuels growth while putting pressure on local domestic producers.

questions.question: The rise of social media platforms has enabled movements for social and political change to gain support across national borders. This phenomenon is best analyzed as an impact of globalization on:
options: The global supply chain.
Cultural homogeneity.
Political and social interconnectedness.
National sovereignty.
questions.answer: Political and social interconnectedness.
questions.explanation: Transnational social media activism strengthens cross-border political and social interconnectedness.

questions.question: A financial crisis that starts in one country's housing market but quickly spreads to affect banks and economies around the world is a real-world illustration of:
options: National economic resilience.
Financial integration and interdependence.
Localized market failure.
Economic diversification.
questions.answer: Financial integration and interdependence.
questions.explanation: Because global banking and capital markets are tightly linked (as in 2008), a national housing crash spreads worldwide.

questions.question: The debate over whether fast food chains and Hollywood movies are leading to a loss of local traditions and customs in different countries is a classic example of the conflict between:
options: Economic liberalization and protectionism.
Cultural globalization and cultural preservation.
Technological advancement and human interaction.
Political integration and national identity.
questions.answer: Cultural globalization and cultural preservation.
questions.explanation: Global consumer media creates tension between cultural diffusion/homogenization and preserving indigenous traditions.

questions.question: Assuming that in the near future, a massive solar flare permanently destroys the internet and all modern satellite communication. Despite this, after 10 years, small groups of people begin traveling long distances on foot to trade rare materials, while others move across borders seeking better farmland or spreading new philosophical ideas. Based on the Hardwire Theory of globalization, how would you interpret this post-internet world phenomenon?
options: Globalization has officially ended because the 'technological hardware' (the internet) that defined it is gone.
This is a 'New Era' of globalization because humans are forced to reinvent the concept of trade from scratch.
Globalization is still active because the 'hardwiring' lies in human urges—like trade and migration—not in the specific tools used to achieve them.
This represents a 'Cycles Theory' peak, where humanity has decided to start a new wave of global connection after a period of isolation.
questions.answer: Globalization is still active because the 'hardwiring' lies in human urges—like trade and migration—not in the specific tools used to achieve them.
questions.explanation: Nayan Chanda's Hardwire Theory attributes globalization to enduring human urges to trade, migrate, preach, and explore.

questions.question: How has economic globalization affected the power of nation-states in the modern interstate system?
options: It has strengthened state sovereignty by reducing foreign influence.
It has made states completely irrelevant in the global economy.
It has eliminated the need for national governments to regulate economies.
It has challenged the autonomy of nation-states due to the influence of multinational corporations and global financial institutions.
questions.answer: It has challenged the autonomy of nation-states due to the influence of multinational corporations and global financial institutions.
questions.explanation: States remain important actors, yet MNCs and IFIs constrain unilateral domestic economic autonomy.

questions.question: In what way did colonization contribute to the early phases of globalization?
options: It reduced global interdependence by making colonies self-reliant.
It isolated indigenous economies from the global market.
It integrated local economies into global trade networks controlled by colonial powers.
It encouraged equal trade relationships between European powers and colonized regions.
questions.answer: It integrated local economies into global trade networks controlled by colonial powers.
questions.explanation: Colonial empires forcibly linked regional resources and labor into Europe-centered global trade circuits.

questions.question: A country's government deciding to enter a regional free trade agreement, which requires it to lower tariffs on goods from member countries, can be analyzed as a way to:
options: Protect domestic industries from foreign competition.
Reduce its economic ties with its neighbors.
Increase its access to international markets.
Promote nationalistic economic policies.
questions.answer: Increase its access to international markets.
questions.explanation: Lowering tariffs via a regional FTA expands export opportunities and market access among member states.

questions.question: How does the global interstate system reinforce the inequality described in World-Systems Theory?
options: It allows all states equal power through international law.
It is structured in a way that benefits powerful states through institutions like the UN and WTO.
It forces core countries to redistribute wealth equally.
It isolates core countries from global trade to protect their interests.
questions.answer: It is structured in a way that benefits powerful states through institutions like the UN and WTO.
questions.explanation: Powerful core states heavily shape rules inside major international institutions.

questions.question: According to World-Systems Theory, which of the following best explains why core countries maintain dominance over peripheral countries?
options: Core countries have more natural resources than peripheral countries.
Peripheral countries choose to remain underdeveloped for cultural reasons.
Core countries control capital, technology, and set the terms of global trade, keeping peripheral countries dependent.
Peripheral countries voluntarily transfer their wealth to core countries through aid programs.
questions.answer: Core countries control capital, technology, and set the terms of global trade, keeping peripheral countries dependent.
questions.explanation: Core dominance stems from controlling advanced technology, capital, and favorable trade terms.

questions.question: Which of the following scenarios best reflects a semi-peripheral country's role in the world-systems framework?
options: A country with no industry that relies entirely on exporting agricultural goods.
A highly developed nation that controls major global financial markets.
A country with some industrialization that both exports labor and manufactures goods for core countries.
A state that isolates itself from the global economy and refuses to trade internationally.
questions.answer: A country with some industrialization that both exports labor and manufactures goods for core countries.
questions.explanation: Semi-peripheral states occupy the middle tier—partly industrialized and linking core capital with peripheral labor/resources.

questions.question: Prime Wear Inc., a sustainable clothing company headquartered in Sweden, designs eco-friendly active wear. The organic cotton is sourced from India, spun into yarn there, shipped to Vietnam for fabric production and sewing, sent to Germany for quality inspection and final packaging, and distributed worldwide through hubs in Europe and North America. How is Prime Wear Inc. participating in the global value chain?
options: By producing all goods locally to reduce transportation costs and promote sustainability
By integrating vertically to maintain full control over every stage of the supply chain in one country
By coordinating production stages across multiple countries to maximize efficiency and cost-effectiveness
By limiting production to countries with the strictest environmental regulations
questions.answer: By coordinating production stages across multiple countries to maximize efficiency and cost-effectiveness
questions.explanation: Fragmenting design, sourcing, sewing, inspection, and distribution across specialized countries defines a Global Value Chain.

questions.question: HoboTech Solutions, a growing mobile app company based in Canada, contracts a third-party firm in India to handle 24/7 customer service and bug reporting across Asia and Europe, allowing HoboTech to focus on app development and marketing. What is the most likely reason HoboTech chose to outsource its customer support operations?
options: To eliminate all customer support functions and automate everything
To access skilled labor at lower costs and provide round-the-clock support across time zones
To permanently relocate its headquarters to India for tax benefits
To avoid complying with Canadian labor laws for tech workers
questions.answer: To access skilled labor at lower costs and provide round-the-clock support across time zones
questions.explanation: BPO outsourcing leverages specialized labor cost advantages and global time-zone coverage.

questions.question: Country A consistently exports more goods and services than it imports (trade surplus), accumulating large foreign currency reserves. Country B imports far more than it exports (trade deficit), relying on foreign loans and investment. Which best explains the economic implications of this relationship?
options: Country A's trade surplus weakens its currency, while Country B's trade deficit strengthens its economy.
Country A's surplus allows it to invest globally and influence other economies, while Country B risks debt accumulation and reduced economic sovereignty.
Trade surpluses always indicate a struggling economy, while trade deficits show economic strength and self-reliance.
Both countries benefit equally from the arrangement because trade automatically balances itself in the long run.
questions.answer: Country A's surplus allows it to invest globally and influence other economies, while Country B risks debt accumulation and reduced economic sovereignty.
questions.explanation: Persistent surpluses build reserve leverage, whereas chronic deficits increase external debt and vulnerability.

questions.question: Three neighboring countries—Country A (agricultural exports), Country B (manufacturing), and Country C (high-tech services)—enter a regional trade agreement removing tariffs, increasing cross-border investments, interconnecting supply chains, and lowering consumer prices. What does this scenario most clearly illustrate about market integration?
options: Market integration increases the isolation of national economies to protect domestic industries.
Market integration reduces economic specialization and creates self-sufficient national markets.
Market integration facilitates economic interdependence through the removal of trade barriers and shared access to goods and services.
Market integration prevents regional cooperation in order to maintain competition among neighboring countries.
questions.answer: Market integration facilitates economic interdependence through the removal of trade barriers and shared access to goods and services.
questions.explanation: Removing tariffs and integrating supply chains boosts specialization, interdependence, and shared market access.
